title: Mirai Botnet Investigation
description: Investigate a Mirai botnet targeting Realtek and Huawei routers.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Welcome to the Mirai Botnet Investigation scenario. Your mission is to investigate a Mirai botnet targeting Realtek and Huawei routers.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the cloud sandbox using your provided credentials.
levels.local_content: Launch Vagrant to start the local sandbox.

levels.title: Identify suspicious beacon service
levels.content:
Analyze network traffic on the `c2-server` host to identify a potential beaconing service used by the Mirai botnet.

Indicators:
- Process name: Hilix[0-9]+.sh
- File or payload name: Hilix[0-9]+.sh
levels.solution: Use `netstat -an` to view active connections, then filter for the process name 'Hilix[0-9]+.sh'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for unusual outbound connections or processes related to the malware indicators of compromise (IOCs).

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the `/var/log/syslog` or `/var/log/messages` for any suspicious activity related to the malware IOCs.

levels.title: Identify suspicious flood service
levels.content:
Investigate network traffic on the `bot1` and `bot2` hosts to identify a potential flood service used by the Mirai botnet for DDoS attacks.

Indicators:
- Process name: flood.sh
levels.solution: Use `netstat -an` to view active connections, then filter for the process name 'flood.sh'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for unusual outbound connections or processes related to the malware indicators of compromise (IOCs).

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the `/var/log/syslog` or `/var/log/messages` for any suspicious activity related to the malware IOCs.

levels.title: Block C2 communication
levels.content:
Configure a firewall rule on the `router` host to block communication between the botnet members (`bot1`, `bot2`) and the command-and-control server (`c2-server`).

Indicators:
- Port number associated with the blocked communication.
levels.solution: Use `iptables` to create a rule that blocks traffic from `bot1` and `bot2` to `c2-server` on port 80.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the C2 IP addresses provided in the MISP event as a starting point.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Consult the `iptables` documentation for more information on creating rules.
